title: S921 (2023-2024 Session) — Const. Am./Require Photo ID For All Voters. (short title); long title: AN ACT TO AMEND THE NORTH CAROLINA CONSTITUTION TO REQUIRE ALL VOTERS TO PRESENT PHOTOGRAPHIC IDENTIFICATION BEFORE VOTING, NOT JUST THOSE PRESENTING TO VOTE IN PERSON.
operative_text:
(a_in_person_id) (section) Secs. 1-2 (amend N.C. Const. art. VI, sec. 2(4) and sec. 3(2)); text covers voters generally, not only in person
(quote) SECTION 1. Section 2(4) of Article VI of the Constitution of North Carolina reads as rewritten: "(4) Photo identification for voting in person. voting. Voters offering to vote in person shall present photographic identification before voting. The General Assembly shall enact general laws governing the requirements of such photographic identification, which may include exceptions."
SECTION 2. Section 3 of Article VI of the Constitution of North Carolina reads as rewritten: "Sec. 3. Registration; Voting in Person.Voting. …
(2) Voters offering to vote in person shall present photographic identification before voting. The General Assembly shall enact general laws governing the requirements of such photographic identification, which may include exceptions."
(b_no_id_remedy) (x) not stated (the amendment text says the General Assembly shall enact laws on the ID requirements, "which may include exceptions"; it sets no remedy)
(c_mail_ballot_id) (section) Sec. 3 (ballot question says the requirement covers all voters, not just in-person voters; the amendment text itself does not mention mail voting)
(quote) SECTION 3. The amendment set out in Sections 1 and 2 of this act shall be submitted to the qualified voters of the State at the statewide general election to be held on November 3, 2026, which election shall be conducted under the laws then governing elections in the State. The question to be used in the voting systems and ballots shall be: "[ ] FOR [ ] AGAINST Constitutional amendment to require all voters, not just those presenting to vote in person, to present photo identification before voting."
(d_proof_of_citizenship) (x) not stated
(e_signature_or_records_verification) (x) not stated
(other_subjects)
Sec. 3 submission to voters at the statewide general election on November 3, 2026 with the ballot question; Sec. 4 State Board certification and Secretary of State enrollment if a majority votes for; Sec. 5 effective upon certification; Sec. 6 effective when it becomes law except as otherwise provided.
Quote for Secs. 4-5:
(other_subjects) (section) Secs. 4-5
(quote) SECTION 4. The State Board of Elections shall certify the results of the referendum conducted under Section 3 of this act. If a majority of votes cast on the question are in favor of the amendment set out in Sections 1 and 2 of this act, the Secretary of State shall enroll the amendment among the permanent records of that office. If a majority of votes cast on the question are against the amendment set out in Sections 1 and 2 of this act, the amendment shall have no effect.
SECTION 5. If the certification from the State Board of Elections under Section 4 of this act reflects that a majority of votes cast on the question are in favor of the amendment set out in Sections 1 and 2 of this act, the amendment set out in Sections 1 and 2 of this act is effective upon certification.
(status) Last Action: Ch. SL 2024-58 on 12/13/2024. Notes had it right: a constitutional amendment requiring photo ID from all voters; number and session confirmed.
(veto_override) Not applicable: constitutional amendments do not go to the Governor; the bill page shows no veto.
(strike_through) PDF extraction drops strike-through, so struck words appear inline. In the Sec. 1 and Sec. 2 quotes the words "voting in person.", "offering to vote in person" (twice) and the heading words "Voting in Person." are struck in the original (confirmed from RTF tracked-change marks, listed below). The amended text therefore reads: "(4) Photo identification for voting. Voters shall present photographic identification before voting." and "(2) Voters shall present photographic identification before voting." The title and ballot question were not struck. I could not confirm the struck words from the PDF alone.
